policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'said unto him': qere אֵלָיו and ketiv אלו are orthographic variants of the same 3ms 'to him'; the English does not distinguish them. Base qere fallback retained.
ASV 'to inquire': qere לִשְׁאָל and ketiv לשאול differ only in plene/defective spelling of the same infinitive; the English does not distinguish them. Base qere fallback retained.

ASV 'did not disclose it to me' renders the idiom 'uncover my ear' with the first-person suffix of the qere אָזְנִי; the ketiv אזנו 'his ear' would give 'to him', which the ASV does not read. The hebrew_gloss note 'runners' concerns 'guard' and does not bear on this unit.
ASV 'Doeg': qere דוֹאֵג and ketiv דויג are spelling variants of the same proper name, both transliterated Doeg; the English does not distinguish them. Base qere fallback retained.
ASV 'Doeg the Edomite': qere דוֹאֵג and ketiv דויג are spelling variants of the same proper name; the English does not distinguish them. Base qere fallback retained.
